title: Ringed pro-etale open-closed localization
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion with complementary quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $A$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site], and use $i^{-1}A,j^{-1}A$ on $Z,U$. The inverse images and direct images are those of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and $j_!$ is the sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the extension-by-zero presheaf [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]: the presheaf value at $V\to X$ is the given module evaluated at $V\to U$ if this factorization exists, and is zero otherwise. The localization of sites is [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], with their induced module actions [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The module functor $j_!$ is left adjoint to $j^{-1}$. These functors satisfy $i^{-1}i_*\cong\operatorname{id}$, $j^{-1}j_!\cong\operatorname{id}$, $j^{-1}i_*=0$, and $i^{-1}j_!=0$. The functors $j_!$ and $i_*$ are exact. For every $A$-module sheaf $M$ the counit and unit give a short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] $0\to j_!j^{-1}M\to M\to i_*i^{-1}M\to0$. If $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $i_*$ commutes with small filtered colimits of module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit, def-weil-size-convention].

proof.text: Use clause (1) and the monomorphism clause (4) of the weakly-etale localization node to identify $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$. For the arbitrary ring sheaf $A$, restriction to this slice is $j^{-1}A$: the inverse-image formula reduces to evaluation on an object already over $U$. Thus the ringed-site restriction/extension adjunction and exactness theorem applies with $\mathcal O=A$. It gives the specified sheafified presheaf, the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$, and exactness of both functors. On objects over $U$ the presheaf is already $G$; every covering of such an object remains over $U$, so sheafification restricts to $G$. The unit $G\to j^{-1}j_!G$ is therefore the identity under this identification. Moreover $(i_*H)(V)=H(V\times_X Z)=H(\varnothing)=0$ for $V\to U$, proving $j^{-1}i_*=0$.

proof.text: Work Zariski locally on $X$, so $X$ and $Z$ are affine. Use the affine ind-etale basis equivalence and the closed-site lift $v$ with base-change functor $u$. The closed-site adjunction node identifies $u(v(W))$ with $W$ for every basis object $W$. Here the inverse-image formula needs no additional lemma: for a basis object $W$, the adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}(W,u(V))=\operatorname{Hom}(v(W),V)$, naturally in $V$. Thus $(v(W),W\to u(v(W)))$ is initial among the pairs indexing the formula, so it is terminal in their opposite category used for the colimit. Every $F(V)$ maps to $F(v(W))$ by restriction along that unique arrow, and these maps identify the colimit with $F(v(W))$, naturally in $W$ and $F$. Sheafification is then exactly the inverse-image definition. Applied to $F=i_*H$, this gives the sheafification of the presheaf $W\mapsto(i_*H)(v(W))=H(u(v(W)))=H(W)$. This is already the restriction of the sheaf $H$ to the basis. The counit is the displayed evaluation map, so its sheafification is the identity. It follows that $i^{-1}i_*H\to H$ is an isomorphism on the basis and hence on the full site, and the counit commutes with restriction to every object over an intersection of affine opens by its naturality. Hence the local isomorphisms are restrictions of one global counit, which is an isomorphism because those opens cover. This argument is for underlying abelian sheaves. Inverse image carries the $A$-action to an $i^{-1}A$-action, and direct image uses $A\to i_*i^{-1}A$; the counit commutes with these actions by naturality of the adjunction with respect to multiplication. Its inverse is consequently linear, proving $i^{-1}i_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ for arbitrary coefficients.

Form the counit $\epsilon:j_!j^{-1}M\to M$ and unit $\eta:M\to i_*i^{-1}M$. The affine covering-family node first gives a cover by affine objects $T=\operatorname{Spec}C$ in the fixed small site. For each such $C$, choose an infinite $\mathcal U$-small cardinal $\kappa\geq |C|$ and apply the bounded ring-extension node. It supplies a one-member pro-etale covering $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\to T$ with $|R|\leq\kappa^{2^{2^{2^\kappa}}}$ and, crucially, retractions of every faithfully flat weakly etale map out of $R$. The bound is still $\mathcal U$-small: a Grothendieck universe is closed under power sets and function sets. Prime ideals, localizations, and the structure sheaf of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ are built from subsets, quotients of pairs, and function sets of $R$, so the resulting affine scheme is $\mathcal U$-bounded; choose its representative in the site's skeleton. Ind-etale maps are weakly etale, and weakly etale maps compose, by the stability node. Thus $V\to X$ is an object of the same small site. These refinements cover every original object by the transitivity axiom of a site. We now use the ring splitting property furnished by the ring-extension statement itself, rather than infer it for unrestricted algebras from small-site weak contractibility. Write $V_Z=V\times_X Z=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$. Clause (3) of the qcqs-morphism permanence node makes the base change $V\times_X U\to V$ of the quasi-compact $j$ quasi-compact. Since $V$ is affine, its inverse image of the affine open $V$ is the whole $V\times_X U=V\setminus V_Z$, which is consequently a quasi-compact open, and $V\setminus V_Z=\bigcup_{f\in I}D(f)$ by the definition of $V(I)$. Basic opens are open; compactness selects finitely many $f_k\in I$ covering this complement, so $V(I)=V(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$. The closed-localization node gives a covering of $V$ by $V_k=\operatorname{Spec}R_{f_k}$ and $V^\sim=\operatorname{Spec}S^{-1}R$, where $S$ consists of elements invertible modulo $I$. On each $V_k$, step 1 identifies $\epsilon$ with the identity and the target of $\eta$ with zero. Every point of $V^\sim$ specializes into its closed fibre, and $S^{-1}R$ is w-contractible; Both $S^{-1}R$ and $R_{f_k}$ are quotients of subsets of $R\times R$, hence remain $\mathcal U$-small; their spectra are bounded by the same subset/function-set argument. The closed-localization covering statement makes their maps to $V$ weakly etale, so the stability node makes the composites to $X$ objects of the same site. Applying the ring-to-site weak-contractibility node to the actual w-contractible ring $S^{-1}R$ and this verified site object shows that $V^\sim$ is weakly contractible on the full small site. The shriek-specialization-zero node makes the source of $\epsilon$ zero there, and the specialization-restriction-sections node identifies $\eta(V^\sim)$ with the identity. These are the actual unit and counit maps, not just abstract identifications of their objects. On this covering family the sequence is therefore either $0\to M\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}M\to0\to0$ or $0\to0\to M\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}M\to0$. The composite vanishes locally and hence globally; kernels and images agree locally and therefore globally, and local lifting of sections proves the last map epic. Forgetting module actions computes these exactness conditions; the maps are linear because the presheaf counit and inverse-image unit commute with multiplication. This proves the claimed short exact sequence without using geometric stalk conservativity.

proof.text: Apply the sequence of step 3 to $M=j_!G$. Step 1 gives $j^{-1}j_!G\cong G$, and the triangle identity makes the first counit $j_!j^{-1}j_!G\to j_!G$ an isomorphism. Its cokernel $i_*i^{-1}j_!G$ is zero. Applying $i^{-1}$ and step 2 gives $i^{-1}j_!G=0$. To prove $i_*$ exact, it is left exact as a right adjoint. Given an epimorphism $H\to H'$ of $i^{-1}A$-modules, let $Q=\operatorname{coker}(i_*H\to i_*H')$. Exactness of $i^{-1}$ and $j^{-1}$ and steps 1 and 2 imply $i^{-1}Q=0$ and $j^{-1}Q=0$. The sequence of step 3 for $Q$ is $0\to0\to Q\to0\to0$, so $Q=0$. Thus $i_*H\to i_*H'$ is epic, and $i_*$ is exact.

proof.text: Assume $X$ qcqs. Test the filtered-colimit comparison on affine objects $V\to X$, which cover every object by the contractible covering-family node. Both $V$ and its closed subscheme $V_Z$ are qcqs. The sections clause (only the first clause) of the qcqs section-calculus node gives filtered-colimit commutation for abelian sheaves on $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $(V_Z)_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Restrictions to these localized sites preserve colimits: they are left adjoints by inverse-image adjunction, and their coefficients are the restricted ring sheaves. For fixed coefficients, the underlying abelian sheaf of a filtered colimit of modules is the abelian sheaf colimit: the presheaf colimit carries the action $a\,[s]=[as]$, well defined by filteredness, and module sheafification has the underlying abelian sheafification and the stated universal property. Hence the abelian sections theorem applies to these module colimits. Using the direct-image formula, at every affine $V$ the comparison is the identity between $\varinjlim_t H_t(V_Z)$ and itself: $(\varinjlim_t i_*H_t)(V)=\varinjlim_t H_t(V_Z)=(i_*\varinjlim_t H_t)(V)$. The identification uses exactly the colimit coprojections and is linear; the comparison is therefore an isomorphism on a covering basis and hence a sheaf isomorphism. No commutation of sections at arbitrary non-qc objects is asserted.
